METADATA.title: What Lowers A Vintage Guitar's Value? Repairs And Changes
METADATA.description: See how refinishes, repairs and replaced parts affect vintage guitar value. I'll explain the comparisons, routine maintenance and what to leave alone.

acceptedAnswer.text: A quality refret generally means 5 to 10 percent less than a comparable original. I treat it as accepted maintenance, while checking the workmanship and the condition of the fretboard.

mainEntity.name: Does A Professionally Repaired Headstock Still Hurt Value?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. A professionally repaired headstock break generally means 40 to 50 percent less than a comparable original. Stable, careful work helps the guitar remain useful, but it doesn't erase the break.

mainEntity.name: Should I Put The Original Parts Back On Before Selling?

acceptedAnswer.text: Keep removed parts with the guitar and explain what was changed. Don't reinstall them to make the guitar appear untouched. An assessment first can establish what belongs with it and whether any further work makes sense.
It can, particularly when the correct original case is difficult to find. I assess the case with the guitar instead of applying one fixed deduction to every instrument.

mainEntity.name: Can A Modified Vintage Guitar Still Be Worth A Lot?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. The model, period, surviving original material, repairs and playing condition all contribute to the assessment. A clear description of the modifications lets it be compared with the right guitars.

mainEntity.name: Does A Refinish Always Erase Collector Interest?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. A fully refinished guitar generally means 40 to 60 percent less than a comparable original, but it can still interest buyers. The work, remaining original parts and underlying instrument determine the comparison.

PRICE_CLAIMS.text: Some changes don't have a useful general percentage. A small finish touch-up, a missing switch tip, a repaired acoustic crack and a replacement bridge need their own assessment. Giving each a neat deduction without knowing the guitar would suggest a precision that isn't there.
PRICE_CLAIMS.basis: Explicit user ruling or unchanged live-site anchor; no newly researched dollar values.

PRICE_CLAIMS.text: For a full refinish, use 40 to 60 percent less than a comparable original. The comparison is with the finish that guitar actually left the factory wearing. Painting a sunburst guitar a desirable custom color doesn't make it an original custom-color example.
PRICE_CLAIMS.basis: Explicit user ruling or unchanged live-site anchor; no newly researched dollar values.

PRICE_CLAIMS.text: A professionally repaired headstock break generally means 40 to 50 percent less than a comparable original. The headstock is the end of the neck that carries the tuners. Even when the repair is stable and the guitar plays well, its history still differs from an otherwise similar unbroken instrument.
PRICE_CLAIMS.basis: Explicit user ruling or unchanged live-site anchor; no newly researched dollar values.

PRICE_CLAIMS.text: A pickup swap without routing is about 25 percent less than a comparable original as a broad vintage Les Paul reference. A guitar routed for a different pickup is 35 to 40 percent less than a comparable original. Cutting the opening changes the wood as well as the electronics, and putting the old pickup back doesn't replace the wood.
PRICE_CLAIMS.basis: Explicit user ruling or unchanged live-site anchor; no newly researched dollar values.

PRICE_CLAIMS.text: Replaced tuners generally mean 10 to 15 percent less than a comparable original. A replacement set that uses the existing holes is a different case from one fitted after drilling or enlarging the headstock. I look behind the headstock as well as at the tuners themselves.
PRICE_CLAIMS.basis: Explicit user ruling or unchanged live-site anchor; no newly researched dollar values.

PRICE_CLAIMS.text: A good refret generally means 5 to 10 percent less than a comparable original. I treat it as accepted maintenance on a guitar that has been played. It may no longer be a museum example with untouched frets, but that doesn't put it in the same category as a stripped or routed instrument.
PRICE_CLAIMS.basis: Explicit user ruling or unchanged live-site anchor; no newly researched dollar values.
